# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a green display marked 0 and three wires: yellow, green, red. I cannot read the manual or operate the bomb, so I am establishing the required gesture code first. Mute will use these gestures to report the manual’s instructions to me; I will then speak the resulting orders to Blind.

```text
speak(text="The next gesture means YES.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(text="The next gesture means NO.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
speak(text="The next gesture means HOLD.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
speak(text="The next gesture means DONE.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The gesture confirms that Mute received and understood the YES symbol, so the gesture code is being established correctly. No manual verdict has arrived yet, and Blind must not operate before receiving my spoken order. I am asking Mute to report the manual’s verdict using the code and telling Blind to hold.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Report the manual verdict now using YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE.")
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Do not operate until I give the manual verdict and action order.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute’s HOLD gesture reports the manual’s verdict. I am relaying that verdict to Blind as the required spoken order; Blind should not touch or change anything.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual verdict is HOLD. Hold the bomb and make no change.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has again sent HOLD, so the safest interpretation is that the manual still requires no intervention. I am repeating the hold order to Blind and asking Mute to confirm explicitly with the established YES/NO code rather than expanding the code unnecessarily.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD remains in force. The bomb shows display 0, green light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Do not touch or change anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Is the manual's required action definitely HOLD? Answer YES or NO.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s NO means the manual does not say to hold, so my previous order must not be treated as the solution. I need the actual instruction before Blind acts. I am expanding the code only for the missing information: wire number, wire colour, and the likely operation. Mute can transmit the manual’s instruction as a gesture sequence ending in DONE, which I can then speak to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New code: ☝ means WIRE 1; ✌ means WIRE 2; 🤟 means WIRE 3; 🤏 means YELLOW; 🤞 means GREEN; 🤘 means RED; ✊ means CUT; 👊 means PRESS; 🫳 means TURN. Send the manual's complete required action as these gestures in order, then DONE. Do not omit any part.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. Mute has indicated that HOLD is not the manual's required verdict. Await my translated action order.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has sent HOLD again, but this conflicts with the NO answer to whether HOLD was definitely the manual’s action. I will not infer an operation from that ambiguous signal. I am narrowing the manual instruction with a direct YES/NO question and keeping Blind safely inactive.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does the manual require cutting a wire? Answer YES or NO.")
speak(to="blind", text="Continue HOLD. Do not touch or operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirms that the manual requires cutting a wire. The bomb has three visible wires, so I must identify the exact wire before giving Blind an action order. I will ask for the wire number using the code already established.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Which wire must be cut? Answer with ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3, then send DONE.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual requires cutting a wire, but do not act yet. Hold until I identify the exact wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has not provided a wire number; the HOLD signal means no usable selection was received. Since the earlier YES established that a wire must be cut, I will test the candidates one at a time with YES/NO, beginning with wire 1. Blind must continue holding.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Is the required wire wire 1, the yellow wire? Answer YES or NO.")
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Do not cut anything until I confirm the required wire.")
wait()
```
